AllocSite.description:
One allocation site: a distinct HPROF stack-trace serial, its resolved frame
lines, and the aggregate footprint of the objects allocated there.

AllocSites.description:
Aggregate allocation-site view. `traces_present` is `false` (with an empty
`sites`) when the dump carries no allocation stack-trace info (HotSpot
writes serial 0 when allocation tracking is off) — reported honestly rather
than faked.

AnalysisFlags.description:
Which opt-in analysis passes were enabled when the report was generated.
Used by the viewer to show context-appropriate "not run" messages.

ArrayFillRatio.description: Fill ratio of raw object arrays (non-null slots / length). Additive.

ArraysBySize.description:
Array-length histogram, split by object-arrays vs primitive-arrays, bucketed
by power-of-two element length. Always-on; derived from data already in
memory (no extra heap scan). Zero-length arrays are tallied separately.

BigDropRow.description:
One "big drop" in the dominator tree: a dominator whose retained heap is
much larger than any single child's, i.e. retention concentrates AT this
node rather than flowing to one dominated child. A large drop marks a good
place to start a leak investigation. Additive; not parity-compared.

child_count.description: Number of dominator-tree children of this node.

drop_bytes.description: retained - largest_child_retained: the heap that "drops" here.

largest_child_class.description: display class of the largest child (empty if none).

largest_child_retained.description: Retained heap of the single largest child (0 if no children).

obj_index_1based.description: 1-based object index of the dominator node.

retained.description: Retained heap of the dominator node.

BigDrops.description: The "Big Drops" view: dominators where retained heap concentrates.

rows.description: Qualifying drops, sorted by drop_bytes descending, capped.

threshold.description: The retained-heap threshold (bytes) a dominator had to exceed to qualify.

BiggestCollectionRow.description:
One individual collection instance in the "biggest collections" listing.
Basics (kind/container_class/elements) are always present; the remaining
fields are filled only under `--collections`. Additive.

obj_index_1based.description: 1-based dense object index for Object Graph Explorer navigation.

value_type_breakdown.description:
Top element/value runtime types by count (Level 2). Empty when
`--collections` was off or no element types were tallied.

BiggestCollections.description:
The largest individual collection instances: a combined ranking plus a
per-kind breakdown. Present whenever collections were classified (basics
always; extra columns only under `--collections`). Additive.

BoxedNumberHolder.description:
One holder-class row for the "who holds the most boxed-number references" ranking.
Only populated when `--collections` is also enabled (FieldPlan available).

boxed_refs.description:
Number of object-reference fields pointing at boxed-number instances across all
live instances of this class.

class_name.description:
Fully-qualified class name whose instances hold the most references to boxed
primitive types (Integer, Long, Double, etc.).

BoxedNumberRow.description:
One boxed-number class row (java.lang.Integer, Long, etc.) surfaced in the
Boxed Numbers section. Data derived from the histogram at report-build time.

avg_shallow.description: Average shallow bytes per instance (total_shallow / instances).

pct_of_heap_bp.description: Share of total reachable shallow heap, in integer basis points (100 bp = 1%).

CaptureParams.description: Parameters used when capturing the object graph snapshot.

edge_cap.description: Max edges per object (outbound and inbound).

CategoryRollup.description:
One rollup row in the "Classes by Category" view: a single
classification category (`"jdk"`, `"framework"`, `"other"`, or any
user-defined category name — see `classify.rs`) aggregated over the
class histogram. A bounded reduction (row count <= #distinct categories
actually present in the dump — typically 2-6), so RSS-safe. Sorted by
`shallow` descending (NOT `retained` — see `shallow_pct` doc below for
why). Answers "how much of my heap is actually MY code vs. everything
else" at a glance, and is the basis for per-category histogram/
biggest-classes table splits in the renderers.

class_count.description: Number of distinct classes classified into this category.

retained.description:
Sum of this category's classes' `retained` (histogram column). NOT a
meaningful "share of heap" basis on its own: unlike `shallow`,
`retained` is NOT mutually exclusive across classes (a `HashMap`'s
retained total already includes its backing `Node[]`'s retained
total, so summing retained across many classes legitimately exceeds
total heap size many times over — confirmed empirically: summing
across just 2 categories exceeded total_shallow by 5.6x on a real
dump). Still useful to show as a raw "retained heap classes in this
category are AT LEAST as big as" figure, just not as a percentage.

shallow_pct.description:
This category's SHALLOW share of total reachable heap, in percent
(0-100). Unlike a `retained`-based percentage, shallow bytes are
mutually exclusive across every object, so these percentages
correctly sum to ~100% across all categories — this is the right
basis for "how much of my heap is X" precisely because of that
property. Precomputed so renderers don't need `overview.total_shallow`
in scope just to show a percentage column.

CharArrayWaste.description:
Waste in char[]/byte[] arrays backing Strings. `top` sorted by
wasted_bytes desc, capped. Additive.

CharArrayWasteRow.description:
One wasteful char[] backing a String (String uses fewer bytes than the
array length). Additive.

ClassFieldStats.description: Per-class aggregation of reference-field statistics for a single class.

category.description:
Classification: `"jdk"`, `"framework"`, `"other"`, or a user-defined
category name. Matches `HistRow.category`. Empty string on pre-v11 JSON
(treat as `"other"`).

holders.description:
Top immediate-dominator classes for instances of this class, sorted by
retained desc. Each entry shows which class holds the most retained bytes
of this class. Empty when idom data is unavailable.

CollectionAttribution.description: Container attribution by holder `Class#field`, present only when `--collections` was passed.

tiny_overhead.description:
Class#field pairs owning the most size-{0,1} collections,
ranked by wrapper-overhead bytes.

CollectionContents.description:
Global "what's in your collections" breakdown, one row per collection class.
Present only under `--collections`. Additive.

CollectionContentsRow.description:
One collection *class* (e.g. `java.util.HashMap`) aggregated across all its
instances: instance count, total element/value slots, and the top runtime
element/value types globally. Additive.

CollectionFillRatio.description:
How full collections are (size vs backing-array capacity). `tracked` =
collections actually sampled; `total` = all collections seen (tracked <=
total when a cap was hit). Additive.

CollectionKindSummary.description: Per-kind rollup over all classified collections. Additive.

CollectionKindTable.description: Biggest collections of one kind (e.g. all Maps), ranked. Additive.

CollectionsAnalysis.description: Groups the five collection/array views. Additive.

CollectionsBySize.description:
Histogram of collection element counts (reuses SizeHistogramBucket).
`empty_count` = collections with size 0. Additive.

Component.description: One component (class loader) in the Top Components view.

pct.description:
Retained heap as a percentage of total reachable shallow heap.
May exceed 100% because a component's retained set can overlap with
other components' retained sets (retained is a transitive closure,
not a partition of the heap).

pct_of_retained.description:
Retained heap as a percentage of the sum of all per-class histogram
retained sizes. Stays ≤ 100% in practice and is easier to interpret.

retained.description: Total retained heap attributed to this component.

top_classes.description: Top classes within this component by retained heap (capped).

ComponentClass.description: One class row inside a component.

ConstantArrayRow.description:
One group of primitive arrays that all hold a single repeated value.
Additive.

is_jdk.description:
True when the array class belongs to the JDK or stdlib (java.*, sun.*, jdk.*, etc.).
Added in cache version 33; older cached JSON has this absent — treated as false by the UI.

owner.description:
Dominant incoming reference (`Class#field`) across the group's member
arrays. `None` when `--collections` was off or no field holds them.

ConstantPrimitiveArrays.description:
Primitive arrays whose every element is the same constant. `truncated` =
true when the distinct-group cap was hit and remaining groups were folded
into one "other" row. Additive.

CulpritBasis.description:
Why a `CulpritRef` was resolved the way it was — lets a consumer (or a
test) distinguish "there's a single standout retainer" from "there are
several comparable ones" from "nothing stands out" without re-deriving the
ranking logic.

oneOf.description:
One suspect's retained share crosses the dominant-culprit threshold —
unambiguously the headline story.

Multiple suspects are independently significant (a compound/multi-leak
dump) — each gets its own `CulpritRef`, none individually dominant.

CulpritRef.description:
A resolved "who's actually responsible" answer, distinct from the raw
`Suspect` list: where `Suspect.pretty_class` is always the TOP-LEVEL
dominator (often a GC-root holder like `Thread` or a static-field owner
that merely transits the real structure), `class_name` here is the
refined pick from that suspect's `path` — the deepest step that is still
"basically the whole problem" (>= `CULPRIT_PATH_RETAINED_PCT` of the
suspect's own retained size) and is not a bare JDK collection-internal
backing structure (`Object[]`, `HashMap$Node[]`, etc.), so the headline
names the actionable application-level class instead of an implementation
detail. Computed once in `build.rs` (see `resolve_primary_culprits`) and
read by the `HeadlineRetainer`/`Concentration`/`DominantGcRootType` triage
rules instead of each re-deriving their own notion of "the culprit".

class_name.description:
The refined class name (see struct docs) — what the headline should
actually name, not necessarily the suspect's own top-level class.

retained.description:
Raw retained bytes at the resolved path step (may be smaller than the
suspect's own `retained` if resolution descended past the top-level
dominator into a more specific class).

retained_pct.description:
Percentage (0-100) of total reachable heap this culprit's retained
size accounts for.

suspect_index.description: `Report.leaks.suspects` index this culprit was resolved from.

DepthBucket.description:
One bucket of the dominator-depth histogram (B2): how many reachable objects
sit exactly `depth` idom-hops below the virtual root.

DomTreeNode.description:
One node of the FULL multi-level dominator subtree rooted at an accumulation
point. Children are the nodes immediately dominated by
this one, sorted retained-desc (tie: obj index asc), bounded by the
`--detail` max-nodes / max-depth caps.

DominatedRow.description:
One immediately-dominated child of an accumulation point (a row of the
"Accumulated Objects in Dominator Tree" list).

DominatorAnalysis.description:
Always-on dominator-tree analysis grouping Big Drops (#1) and Immediate
Dominators (#2), mirroring Eclipse MAT's dominator views. Additive.

longest_chain_depth.description:
Longest path in the dominator tree (number of idom-hops from the virtual
root to the deepest node). A value > 10,000 indicates a linked-list-shaped
data structure. 0 for an empty heap. V25.

DupArrayHolder.description:
One holder-class row for the "who holds the most duplicate arrays" ranking.
Only populated when `--collections` is also enabled (FieldPlan available).

array_refs.description:
Number of object-reference fields pointing at duplicate arrays across all
instances of this class.

class_name.description:
Fully-qualified class name whose instances hold the most references to
duplicate primitive arrays.

DupPrimArrayRow.description: One element-type row in the duplicate-primitive-array breakdown.

duplicated_groups.description: Number of distinct content groups that have at least one duplicate.

wasted_bytes.description:
Total wasted bytes for this element type:
Σ over duplicated groups of `(count - 1) * shallow`.

DupPrimArrays.description:
Approximate duplicate-primitive-array analysis. Top-N per-type breakdown
sorted by wasted bytes descending.

rows.description: Per-element-type breakdown, sorted by wasted_bytes descending, capped.

top_array_holders.description:
Top-N classes whose instances hold the most references to duplicate arrays.
Populated only when `--collections` is also on (requires a FieldPlan scan).

total_wasted_bytes.description: Total wasted bytes across all element types.

DupStringSample.description:
One of the most-duplicated String values: its exact text (truncated to
`MAX_STR_SAMPLE` bytes), how many String instances share the value, the
decoded byte length of the value, and the approximate wasted bytes.

count.description: Number of String instances sharing this value.

len.description: Decoded byte length of the value (pre-truncation).

text.description: Exact decoded text, truncated to at most `MAX_STR_SAMPLE` bytes on a char boundary.

wasted_bytes.description: Approx wasted bytes for this value: (count - 1) * len.

DupStrings.description:
Approximate duplicate-`java.lang.String` analysis. Each String value is
decoded, hashed to a 64-bit value, and only the hash + length + occurrence
count is retained — the decoded bytes are dropped immediately, so RSS stays
bounded regardless of dump size. Hash collisions merge distinct values (an
accepted approximation). The unit of dedup is the String INSTANCE: two
String instances with the same decoded value count as a duplicate even
though they usually hold separate backing arrays. Opt-in via `--find-duplicates`.

approx_wasted_bytes.description: Approx bytes wasted by duplication: Σ over duplicated values of (count-1)*first_seen_len.

char_array_waste.description:
Wasted space in char[]/byte[] arrays backing Strings. `None` unless
`--find-duplicates` computed it.

distinct_values.description: Distinct decoded String values (by 64-bit hash; collisions merge — accepted approximation).

duplicated_values.description: Distinct values that occur in more than one String instance.

length_histogram.description:
Power-of-two histogram of decoded String lengths (bytes), one entry per
distinct value. Sorted by `upper_len` ascending.

top_by_length.description:
Top-N longest distinct String values by decoded byte length, sorted by
len desc then text asc. Only populated with `--find-duplicates`.

top_duplicated.description:
Top-N most-duplicated String values with exact (truncated) text, sorted by
occurrence count desc then text asc. Only values with count > 1.

top_string_holders.description:
Top-N owning classes by the number of `java.lang.String` instances their
instances reference. Sorted by `string_refs` desc then class name asc.

loader_count.description: Number of DISTINCT loader ids this class name appears under (>= 2).

loaders.description: Loader labels (capped) that loaded this class name, for display.

DuplicateClassLoaderRow.description:
One class-loader's contribution to a duplicated class name (see
[`DuplicateClass`]). Additive; not parity-compared.

loader_label.description:
Display label for this loader (e.g. `<boot>` or an app loader), or the
synthesized `loader@0x…` fallback when no label was resolved.

FieldAttributionBiggestRow.description: One holder `Class#field` whose single largest container is ranked by element count.

capacity.description:
Backing-array length (slots) of the single largest container:
`elements` = used, `capacity` = slots. Real for arrays; for classified
collections this equals `elements` (degenerate — see the field-decode
note; the backing array's true length is not cheaply joinable). Additive.

container_kind.description: Kind of the single largest container (same labels as `FieldAttributionRow::container_kind`).

FieldAttributionRow.description: One holder `Class#field` ranked by total elements across every container it points at.

holder_instances.description:
Live-instance count of `holder_class` from the System-Overview class
histogram (matched by prettified class name), or `0` when the holder
class has no histogram row. Additive.

total_wasted_bytes.description:
`total_wasted_slots × object-reference width (bytes)` — the actual bytes
of backing-array capacity that is null/unused. More directly comparable
than slot count when array types differ. Additive.

total_wasted_slots.description:
Sum of (capacity - elements) across all distinct containers reached by
this field. Counts empty slots, not bytes. Zero for classified
collections (their capacity is not cheaply available). Additive.

FieldBySizeRow.description:
One holder `Class#field` (with declared field type) ranked by the total
retained size of everything the field points at, summed over all live
holder instances. Additive.

category.description:
Pointee category: `"collection"`, `"array"`, or `"object"`, derived from
the dominant runtime pointee type. Additive.

elements.description:
Total element count over container pointees of this field (`0` for
non-container fields). Additive.

holder_instances.description: Live-instance count of `holder_class` from the class histogram, or `0`.

pointee_type.description:
Runtime class of what the field points at (dominant type by retained
size). HPROF does not record declared reference-field types, so this is
the concrete pointee class; `varies` when the field points at multiple
types and no single one dominates.

pointees.description: Number of distinct pointees (non-null field slots) for this field.

total_retained.description: Sum of retained size over distinct pointees of this `Class#field`.

FieldRefStat.description:
Per-class reference-field statistics: null/non-null ref counts and total
retained size of pointees. Populated only when `--field-stats` is passed.

total_retained.description: Sum of retained[] for all non-null pointees.

FieldStats.description:
Collection of per-class reference-field stats, present only when
`--field-stats` was passed.

FieldsBySize.description:
`Class#field` holders ranked by total retained size of their pointees.
Present only when `--collections` was passed. Additive.

FillRatioBucket.description:
One bucket of a fill-ratio (used/capacity) histogram. Ratio expressed in
basis points (0..=10000). Additive.

FinalizerClassRow.description:
One entry in the Finalizer referents breakdown: the class name of the
referent (the object that `finalize()` will be called on) and how many
live `java.lang.ref.Finalizer` instances wrap it.

count.description: Number of live `java.lang.ref.Finalizer` instances with this referent class.

referent_class.description: Pretty class name of the finalizer referent.

retained.description: Total retained heap of the referent objects.

instance_count.description: Count of live instances of the sentinel class (or subclasses).

total_retained.description: Total retained heap across all sentinel class instances, in bytes.

GcRootClassRow.description: One class entry within a GC-root-retained-by-type row.

GcRootRetainedRow.description: One row of the GC-root-retained-by-type table.

top_classes.description: Top-5 retained classes for this root type (class name, count, retained bytes).

GcRootTypeRow.description:
One row of the GC-roots-by-type breakdown: a human-readable root-type label
and how many roots carry that HPROF type.

HeaderOverheadRow.description:
One row of the Object Header Overhead breakdown: classes where object headers
(12 or 16 bytes each, depending on compressed OOPs) are a significant fraction
of the class's total shallow heap. Data derived from the histogram.

avg_shallow.description: Average shallow bytes per instance (class's total shallow / instances).

header_bytes.description: Object header size in bytes for this JVM: 12 (compressed OOPs / 32-bit) or 16.

header_pct_of_shallow_bp.description:
Header overhead as a share of the class's total shallow heap,
in integer basis points (100 bp = 1%).

total_header_bytes.description: `instances * header_bytes` — total bytes consumed by headers for this class.

HeapComposition.description:
B5: reachable-heap composition split by object kind (instances vs. arrays
vs. class objects). Rows are in fixed kind order; empty buckets are omitted.

prim_array_by_type.description:
When primitive arrays are present, further split by element type
(e.g. "byte[]", "int[]"). Omitted when empty or only one type.

HistRow.description: One row of the System-Overview class histogram (full, one row per class).

category.description:
Classification category this class falls into (`"jdk"`, `"framework"`,
`"other"`, or any user-defined category name from `.hprof-analyzer.toml`'s
`[[category]]` entries / `--category` flags). See `classify.rs`. Always
present; defaults to `"other"` for synthetic rows the classifier never
saw. `#[serde(default)]` so pre-v14 JSON (which lacks the field) still
deserializes as `""` — renderers should treat an empty string the same
as `"other"`.

incoming_ref_count.description:
Total number of inbound references (edges) pointing at instances of this
class across all captured objects. Answers "how many objects hold a ref to
an instance of this class?" Same semantics as JProfiler's incoming-ref count
in the histogram. Always present; `0` for synthetic rows (no backing objects).

loader_id.description:
Class-loader object address that loaded this class (0 = boot loader).
Distinct (class, loader) pairs are distinct rows, matching MAT's
class-object-identity histogram keying.

loader_label.description:
Human-readable label for `loader_id`: the class NAME of the loader
object (e.g. `jdk/internal/loader/ClassLoaders$AppClassLoader`), or
`<boot>` for the boot loader (address 0). `None` when the loader address
could not be resolved (e.g. leak-suspect `dominated_by_class` rows where
the histogram-row index is not readily available). Purely descriptive —
NOT parity-gated and never compared numerically.

max_instance_shallow.description:
Shallow size of the single largest instance of this class — surfaces a
lone oversized object hiding behind a small instance count. `0` for
synthetic rows that have no backing object (the injected system class
loader, leak-suspect `dominated_by_class` rows). `#[serde(default)]` so
pre-v5 reports (which lack the field) still deserialize.

root_path.description:
Dominator chain from the highest-retained instance of this class up to its
GC root. Populated for the top-20 histogram rows by retained heap in the
System Overview. `None` for synthetic rows (no backing objects) and for
rows outside the top-20. Additive; `#[serde(default)]` so older JSON still
deserializes.

HolderRow.description: One holder-class entry in the `ClassRow.holders` breakdown.

count.description: Number of instances of the target class dominated by this holder class.

holder_class.description: Class name of the immediate dominator.

level2.description:
Top immediate dominators of this holder class (level 2). Empty when
holder is a GC root or level-2 data was not available.

retained.description: Sum of retained heap of those instances.

via_class.description:
Intermediate classes on a multi-hop synthesised holder chain, ordered
from the direct dominator toward the target. Empty for direct holders.
For example, if the chain is `HashMap → HashMap$Node[] → HashMap$Node`,
the `HashMap` HolderRow for `HashMap$Node` has
`via_class = ["HashMap$Node[]"]`. Three-hop example:
`A → B → C → Target` → `via_class = ["B", "C"]` on the `A` row.

ImmDomPair.description:
One (dominator_class, dominated_class) pair for the V5 two-sided sankey.
Powers "who holds X" (rows where dominated_class == target) and
"what does X hold" (rows where dominator_class == target) from a single dataset.

dominated_retained.description: Aggregate retained heap of the dominated objects.

dominated_shallow.description: Aggregate shallow heap of the dominated objects.

pair_count.description: Number of (dominator, dominated) object pairs counted.

top_app_dominator.description:
First ancestor in the idom chain of objects in this pair (walking up
from the dominator side) whose category is not `jdk` or `framework`.
Empty when the dominator is already non-JDK/framework.

ImmediateDominatorRow.description:
One row of the immediate-dominator class rollup: for each dominator class,
how many objects it immediately dominates and their aggregate shallow heap.

dominated_count.description: Number of objects immediately dominated by objects of this class.

dominated_shallow.description: Aggregate shallow heap of the dominated objects.

dominator_count.description: Number of distinct dominator objects of this class (with >=1 dom child).

dominator_shallow.description: Aggregate shallow heap of those dominator objects.

top_app_dominator.description:
First ancestor in the dominator chain whose category is not `jdk` or
`framework` — i.e. the closest user-visible class retaining these
objects. Empty when the dominator is already non-JDK/framework.

ImmediateDominators.description:
The "Immediate Dominators" view: dominated-object rollup keyed by the
dominator's class. Additive; not parity-compared.

pairs.description:
Per-(dominator_class, dominated_class) pairs for the two-sided sankey.
Sorted by dominated_retained descending, capped at IMDOM_PAIRS_CAP.
Additive; defaults to empty for round-trip with older JSON.

pairs_total_count.description:
Total number of distinct (dominator_class, dominated_class) pairs before
capping. Equals `pairs.len()` when not truncated. Additive.

pairs_truncated.description: True when `pairs` was capped and some pairs were dropped. Additive.

rows.description: Rows sorted by dominated_shallow descending, capped.

InboundEdge.description: One inbound reference captured in the static report snapshot.

field_name.description: Field name on `src` that points to this node, or "" if unnamed.

src_idx.description: Dense index of the object holding the reference to this node.

KindStat.description: One kind-bucket of the heap-composition breakdown (B5).

LeakIndicators.description:
Scalar indicators of common Java leak patterns. All fields are always
computed; zero when the corresponding objects are absent.

anonymous_class_count.description:
Count of anonymous/generated class definitions (names matching `$\d+`,
`$$Lambda$`, `$$Anon`, or `$Proxy` patterns).

direct_byte_buffer_cap_buckets.description:
Capacity distribution of live DirectByteBuffers across 8 buckets:
`[<1 KB, 1–4 KB, 4–16 KB, 16–64 KB, 64–256 KB, 256 KB–1 MB, 1–16 MB, ≥16 MB]`.
All zeros when no DirectByteBuffers are present.

direct_byte_buffer_capacity_sum.description:
Sum of `capacity` fields across all live `DirectByteBuffer` instances,
representing total off-heap memory tracked by live NIO buffers.

direct_byte_buffer_count.description:
Count of live `DirectByteBuffer` instances. Paired with
`direct_byte_buffer_capacity_sum` to compute average buffer capacity.
0 when no DirectByteBuffers are present or the class was not found.

nio_buffer_owners.description:
Top NIO buffer owners (dense_idx, capacity) sorted by capacity descending.
At most 20 entries. Empty when no DirectByteBuffers are present.

thread_local_null_key_count.description:
Count of `ThreadLocal$ThreadLocalMap$Entry` instances whose referent
(the ThreadLocal key) has been cleared — the classic thread-local leak signal.

LoaderRollup.description:
F2: per-class-loader rollup over the class histogram. One row per distinct
`loader_id`, aggregating the classes it loaded. A bounded reduction over the
histogram (row count <= #loaders), so RSS-safe. Sorted retained-desc.

class_count.description: Number of distinct classes loaded by this loader.

loader_label.description:
Human-readable loader label (class name of the loader object, or
`<boot>`); `None` when the label could not be resolved.

MapCollisionRatio.description:
Hash-map collision proxy (occupied slots vs size); `wasted` in its buckets
is always 0. Additive.

MergedPathNode.description:
One node of a "merged shortest paths to GC roots" prefix tree (Eclipse MAT
"Merge Shortest Paths"): the dominator chains of all members of a class-group
suspect, collapsed by class-at-each-depth. `object_count` is how many member
chains pass through this node; `retained` sums those members' retained heap
contribution at this node. Additive; not parity-compared.

field_edge.description:
Field name on the parent node that points to this child; only present
when `--ref-paths` was set and a consistent field name was found across
all chains that pass through this node.

object_count.description: Number of member chains passing through this node.

retained.description: Aggregate retained heap of the objects represented at this node.

root_type_label.description: GC-root type label when this node is a root (the chain terminus).

NioBufferOwner.description:
Root-path attribution for a large DirectByteBuffer. Mirrors the `RootPathStep`
pattern used by leak suspects to trace who owns a buffer through the dominator tree.

capacity.description: Off-heap capacity of this DirectByteBuffer in bytes.

display_class.description: Display class name of the buffer object.

retained.description: Retained heap bytes of this object (on-heap cost of keeping it alive).

root_path.description: Dominator-tree path from this object up to a GC root.

ObjGraphEdge.description: Outbound edge from one object to another (Reference Graph Explorer / V3).

ObjGraphFlat.description:
Flat lookup table powering V3 + V4 navigation (object graph + dominator explorer).
Only present when --obj-graph is used.

capture_params.description: Capture parameters (tier name, edge_cap) for the UI indicator.

dom_children.description: Immediate dominator children for all significant nodes. Key = parent dense index.

edges.description: Outbound edges for captured nodes. Key = dense index (u32).

inbound_edges.description:
Inbound reference snapshot (who points to each captured node).
Key = dense index (as string in JSON). Only present for nodes in the capture set.

inbound_truncated.description: Dense indices of nodes where inbound edges were truncated at edge_cap.

nodes.description: All significant nodes (retained >= sig_floor_bytes). Key = dense index (u32).

root_dom_trees.description: Pre-built depth-3 dominator trees for top-20 root objects (for SVG mode in V4).

roots.description: Dense indices of dominator roots (idom == vroot).

sig_floor_bytes.description: Minimum retained bytes to be included as a significant node.

ObjGraphFlatNode.description: One node in the flat object graph lookup table.

dom_subtree_count.description: Total number of objects in the dominated subtree rooted here (including self).

subtree_classes.description:
Top-10 classes by shallow heap across the entire dominated subtree (including self).
Omitted when empty (e.g. leaf nodes or small subtrees).

held_via.description:
Stack-frame holding this object (`ClassName#methodName()`), when the
object is a significant local in a thread's stack frame and no field
owner was found. `None` otherwise.

holder_chain.description:
First 1–2 dominator-chain hops toward a GC root (class names only).
`[0]` = immediate dominator class, `[1]` = its immediate dominator.
Empty when the object is a direct GC root.

owner.description:
Dominant incoming reference (`Class#field`) that holds this object.
`None` when `--collections` was off or no attributed field points at it.

pct_bp.description:
Retained share of total reachable shallow heap, in integer basis
points (bp = round(retained / total_shallow * 10000)). Deterministic
integer for JSON output; the Markdown renderer uses `pct` instead.

PackageNode.description:
One node of the pruned package tree (MAT PackageTreeResult parity).
Totals are CUMULATIVE over all top-level dominators in this node's subtree.

children.description: Children sorted retained-desc, tie-broken by name-asc.

name.description: This segment's name (e.g. "util"); the root node's name is "".

retained_heap.description: Cumulative retained heap (sum over the top-level dominators under this node).

shallow_heap.description: Sum of shallow heap of the top-level dominators under this node.

top_dominator_count.description: Number of top-level dominators under this node (MAT "# Objects").

PathStep.description: One step of a single-suspect accumulation path.

PoolInstanceRow.description: Decoded field values for one pool instance (P1).

active_count.description: Active/busy workers at snapshot time. `None` when not available.

max_pool_size.description: Maximum pool size. `None` when the field could not be read.

obj_index_1based.description: 1-based object index of the pool object.

pool_size.description: Core / configured pool size. `None` when the field could not be read.

queue_depth.description:
Task or connection queue depth (from `workQueue.size` or equivalent).
`None` when not available.

PoolSnapshot.description: Pool state snapshot for one pool class — one row per instance.

class_name.description: Fully-qualified class name of the pool sentinel class.

instances.description: Per-instance decoded fields, capped at 20 rows.

total_retained.description: Total retained heap across all instances, in bytes.

PropEntry.description:
One decoded JVM system property (`java.lang.System.props` entry). Serialized
as a stable `{ "key": ..., "value": ... }` object (rather than a positional
array) so the JSON schema is self-describing.

elapsed_ms.description:
Wall-clock milliseconds this query took (parse+plan+run), set by the
server pipeline. Omitted from JSON when absent so the analyze report and
its golden snapshot stay byte-identical.

error.description: Set (with rows empty) when the query failed to parse/plan/execute.

name.description: Query label (e.g. "q1" or a user-supplied name).

note.description:
Optional advisory note (e.g. "edge retention capped"); populated by later
phases, harmless (`None`) otherwise. Omitted from JSON when absent.

truncated.description: True if a cap was hit and rows are a bounded sample.

viz.description:
Optional visualization directive (`-- @viz ...`) declared with the query.
`None` renders a plain table (today's behavior). Omitted from JSON when
absent so no-viz reports are byte-identical.

oneOf.description: A reference to a heap object: dense index + its class name for display.

addr.description:
Heap address of the object, when resolvable. Omitted from JSON when
absent so the analyze golden snapshot (no obj_ref values) stays
byte-identical and non-server callers are unaffected.

gc_root_tag_counts.description: (root sub-tag byte, count), sorted by count desc then tag asc for stable output.

RefStatClassRow.description: One class row in a reference-statistics histogram. Additive.

ReferenceStats.description:
Statistics for one reference kind (Soft/Weak/Phantom). `kind` is the
label. `referent_histogram` = classes of referents grouped/counted.
`only_weakly_retained` = referent classes reachable ONLY through the weak
edge (idom == u32::MAX). Additive.

null_referent_count.description: Number of reference objects whose referent field is null (referent was GC'd).

ReferencesAnalysis.description:
The three reference views, each optional (None when that kind is absent).
Additive.

RetainerRow.description: One row of the merged Top Retainers table (§813).

RetentionSummary.description:
B3: retention concentration over top-level dominators. Basis-point shares
(of total reachable shallow heap) held by the top-1/10/100 objects, plus how
many single objects each hold >=1% of the heap. Answers "one leak or many?".

num_objects_ge_1pct.description: Count of single objects each retaining >=1% of total reachable shallow.

top1_bp.description:
Retained share of the top-1 / top-10 / top-100 top-level dominators, in
integer basis points (100 bp = 1%) of total reachable shallow heap.

top1_retained.description:
Exact retained bytes for the top-1 / top-10 / top-100 top-level dominators.
Derive % from these rather than reconstructing from bp to avoid rounding loss.

RootPathStep.description:
One hop of the dominator chain from a suspect up toward its GC
root. The final hop carries `root_type_label` when the node
is itself a GC root.

field_edge.description:
Name of the field on this object that points to the next hop (parent's
field → child). Only present when `--ref-paths` was set. Empty string
means "no field name available" (class edge, array element, synthetic
thread-local edge).

SelfReferentialClassRow.description:
One class whose instances form a self-referential/recursive structure in
the dominator tree — a meaningful fraction of its own instances have an
ancestor (in the dominator tree) that is ALSO an instance of this same
class (e.g. a `Node` class holding a `List<Node> children` field, so
descending from a root `Node` eventually reaches another `Node`).

Built from the `has_same_class_ancestor` bitset (already computed by
`retained.rs` for the histogram's double-counting guard) — this is the
first place that bitset is exposed as an explicit, per-class, named
signal rather than only being used internally to adjust a sum. See the
`SelfReferentialClassAccumulation` triage rule in triage.rs.

instances.description: Total reachable instances of this class.

nested_instances.description:
How many of those instances have a dominator-tree ancestor that is
also an instance of this same class (or the class-object representing
it) — i.e. are NOT the "root" of their own same-class subtree.

nested_pct.description:
`nested_instances / instances * 100`. High (e.g. >90%) means almost
every instance is nested inside another instance of the same class —
a tree/chain shape, not independent siblings.

retained.description:
This class's retained heap — the SAME number the System-Overview
histogram's `retained` column and `biggest_classes` show (both
already exclude nested same-class-ancestor instances from the sum,
so a deeply self-referential subtree is not double/triple-counted;
see `has_same_class_ancestor` docs in retained.rs). This is why the
floor/ranking here is on RETAINED, not shallow: a `Node` class with
tiny per-instance shallow size (just a couple of reference fields)
but a huge recursively-held payload is exactly the pattern this rule
exists to catch — shallow size alone would miss it entirely.

SignificantFrame.description:
One stack frame plus the significant local-variable objects it retains.
Populated only under `--thread-locals`.

locals.description: Significant local objects held at this frame, retained desc.

SignificantLocal.description: One significant local-variable object held at a frame.

display_class.description: Class name of the local object.

pct.description:
Retained heap as a percentage of total reachable shallow heap (same
basis as every other "% Heap" figure in the report).

retained.description: Retained heap of the local object.

SizeBucket.description:
One power-of-two size bucket of the top-level-dominator retained-size
distribution. `upper_bytes` is the inclusive upper bound (a power of two);
a dominator with retained size r falls in the smallest bucket whose
`upper_bytes >= r`. `count` is how many top-level dominators land here.

SizeHistogramBucket.description:
One power-of-two length bucket in the arrays-by-size histogram. `upper_len`
is the inclusive upper bound of the bucket (a power of two): a bucket with
`upper_len = 8` counts arrays whose element length is in `5..=8`. The first
bucket is `1..=1` (upper_len 1); zero-length arrays are counted separately.

StrLenBucket.description:
One power-of-two bucket of the String-length histogram. `upper_len` is the
inclusive upper bound (a power of two); a value of length `l` falls in the
smallest bucket whose `upper_len >= l`. `count` is the number of distinct
String values in this bucket.

StrLenStats.description: Summary stats over distinct-value String lengths (bytes). `Default` = zeros.

StringHolder.description:
One owning class and how many `java.lang.String` instances its instances
reference (across all object-reference fields).

SubtreeClassRow.description: One class row in a dominator-subtree class breakdown.

Suspect.description: One leak suspect (single large object or class group).

accumulation_obj_1based.description:
The accumulation point object where retained heap piles up (the last
step of `path`). `None` for group suspects or when the descent hit
`MAX_ACCUM_DEPTH` without a big drop.

dominated.description:
Top immediately-dominated children of the accumulation point, sorted
retained-desc and capped at the configured cap. Empty for groups.

dominated_by_class.description:
By-class histogram (objects/shallow/retained) of the accumulation
point's immediately-dominated children, sorted retained-desc and
capped. Empty for groups.

dominated_shown.description:
F3: how many rows the `dominated` list actually shows (== dominated.len()),
so a renderer can say "showing top M of N".

dominated_total_count.description:
F3: FULL count of immediately-dominated children of the accumulation
point (the dominator-children CSR degree, uncapped). The number the
capped `dominated` list cannot convey — "how many objects does this
accumulation point directly hold?". 0 for group suspects / no accum.

dominator_tree.description:
FULL multi-level dominator subtree rooted at the accumulation point.
`None` when the suspect has no accumulation point (skipped in JSON).
Bounded by the `--detail` max-nodes / max-depth caps.

keywords.description:
Class names involved in this suspect (suspect class + accumulation
point class), de-duplicated in first-seen order, for search.

merged_paths.description:
F: merged shortest paths to GC roots for a class-group suspect — the
member objects' dominator chains collapsed into a class-keyed prefix
tree. `None` for single suspects (they already have `root_path`).
Bounded by the `--detail` max-nodes / max-depth caps.

path.description:
Descent from the suspect object to the accumulation point (MAT
`findAccumulationPoint`, big-drop-ratio 0.7). Non-empty only for singles.

root_path.description:
Dominator chain from this single suspect up to its GC root. Only
populated for single suspects; `None` for group suspects (skipped in
JSON). Bounded by the `--detail` root-path max-depth cap.

root_type_label.description:
Human label of the GC-root TYPE holding this suspect (e.g. "Thread",
"Sticky Class", "JNI Global"), when the suspect's top-level dominator is
itself an identifiable single GC root. Empty when unknown: the suspect
is not itself a root, is held by multiple/ambiguous roots, or the root
type is `ROOT_UNKNOWN`. Only populated for single suspects.

boxed_number_holders.description:
Top classes holding the most references to boxed-number objects
(Integer, Long, etc.). Populated only when `--collections` is on.
Additive; not parity-compared.

boxed_numbers.description:
Boxed-number classes (java.lang.Integer, Long, etc.) found in the histogram,
sorted by total shallow heap descending. Empty when no boxed types appear.
Additive; not parity-compared.

classloaders_loaded.description:
Count of DISTINCT class-loader addresses among loaded classes (boot
loader counted once when present). This is "loaders referenced by loaded
classes", NOT MAT's loader-object count — not a parity-gated scalar.

compressed_oops.description:
Whether the JVM used compressed ordinary object pointers: true when
references are narrower than identifiers (8-byte id, 4-byte ref). None
when undeterminable. Not applicable (false) for 32-bit dumps.

dominator_depth_histogram.description:
B2: dominator-depth histogram (retention shape). depth = idom-hops to the
virtual root. Sorted by depth ascending. Always present; empty only for
an empty heap. Surfaced in OOM Triage as a synthesized "Shape" line; the
full histogram lives in JSON. Excludes the synthetic system-classloader
object (it has no graph node).

dump_creation.description:
Dump creation time in millis since Unix epoch (HPROF header base
timestamp). None when the header timestamp is absent/zero.

duplicate_classes.description:
F2: class names loaded under more than one loader (duplicate-class /
class-loader-leak signature), capped. Additive. Not parity-compared.

duplicate_prim_arrays.description:
Approximate duplicate-primitive-array analysis, present only when
`--find-duplicates` was passed; `None` otherwise. Additive; not parity-compared.

duplicate_strings.description:
Approximate duplicate-String analysis, present only when `--find-duplicates`
was passed; `None` otherwise. Additive; not parity-compared.

file_path.description: Full path the dump was opened from (superset of `source_name`).

gc_roots_by_type.description:
GC roots broken down by HPROF root type (e.g. "System Class", "Thread",
"JNI Global"), sorted by count descending then label ascending. Excludes
synthetic roots the analyzer injects. Empty only when there are no roots.

gc_roots_retained_by_type.description: Retained heap grouped by GC root type. Additive; empty when no roots.

header_overhead.description:
Per-class object-header overhead: classes where headers account for a large
fraction of shallow heap or represent a large absolute overhead. Top-30
sorted by total_header_bytes descending. Additive; not parity-compared.

heap_composition.description:
B5: reachable-heap composition by object kind. Always present; empty
only for an empty heap.

heap_fragmentation_ratio.description:
Ratio of unreachable shallow heap to total heap (reachable + unreachable).
Range [0.0, 1.0]. 0.0 for an empty heap.

histogram_truncated_to.description:
Number of histogram rows the full histogram was capped to, or None when
the histogram is complete (never truncated). Always None today.

identifier_size_bits.description: HPROF identifier size in BITS (id_size bytes * 8: 32 or 64).

jvm_version.description:
Derived JVM version (prefers `java.vm.version`, else `java.version`).
None when neither property was decoded. Additive: not parity-compared.

loader_rollup.description:
F2: per-loader rollup over the histogram, top-N by retained heap.
Additive bounded reduction (<= #loaders rows). Not parity-compared.

record_census.description:
HPROF record census: raw record-type counts for the dump (UTF8,
LOAD_CLASS/UNLOAD_CLASS, stack frames/traces, heap segments, per-object
dumps, per-GC-root-tag). Additive; not parity-compared. Carried from
pass1 counters via the graph. `#[serde(default)]` so pre-v5 reports
(which lack the field) still deserialize.

retention_concentration.description:
B3: retention concentration over top-level dominators. Always present
(zeroed for an empty heap). Surfaced in OOM Triage as a "One leak or
many" line.

system_properties.description:
Decoded JVM system properties (java.lang.System static `props`), sorted
by key. Empty when the props object is absent or its layout could not be
safely decoded (graceful fallback — never garbage). Additive: not
parity-compared.

top_class_concentration_bp.description:
Retained heap share of the single largest class, in integer basis points (100 bp = 1%).
0 for an empty heap.

unreachable_composition.description:
Composition of the unreachable heap by object kind (instances / object
arrays / primitive arrays / class objects), mirroring `heap_composition`
for the reachable heap. Additive; not parity-compared. Empty when there
are no unreachable objects.

unreachable_dominator_skipped.description:
True when the unreachable dominator pass was skipped because the unreachable
set exceeded the threshold. The unreachable histogram shows shallow-by-class
instead of retained-by-class; garbage_roots is empty.

unreachable_garbage_roots.description:
Top garbage-root dominator subtrees in the unreachable forest, sorted by
retained desc and capped (top-5 roots × depth-4). Each entry is the root
of a subtree of unreachable objects with no reachable predecessor; the
tree structure reflects the dominator relationships within that garbage
cluster. Additive; not parity-compared.

unreachable_histogram.description:
Per-class histogram of unreachable objects (idom == u32::MAX), sorted by
shallow descending and capped. Additive; not parity-compared.

unreachable_retained.description:
Total retained heap held within the unreachable forest, computed by a
dominator pass over the unreachable subgraph. Equals the sum of shallow
sizes of all unreachable objects (every unreachable object is dominated
by exactly one garbage root within the forest). Additive; not parity-
compared. 0 when there are no unreachable objects.

ThreadInfo.description:
A single thread's call stack, resolved from HPROF STACK_TRACE/STACK_FRAME
records. Identifies the thread by its heap object (index + class) since the
thread NAME requires decoding java.lang.Thread fields (a later step).

class_name.description:
Class name of the resolved thread object, or None when the thread
object could not be located in the heap.

context_class_loader.description:
Display label of the thread's `contextClassLoader` (e.g.
`java.net.URLClassLoader @ 0x…`), or None when absent/unresolved. Additive.

dominant_retained_class.description:
The class that dominates the most retained heap for this thread — the
single most expensive type reachable from this thread's locals/fields.
Empty when retained heap is zero or thread has no local objects. Additive.

local_objects.description:
Bounded sample of this thread's GC-thread-local root objects (retained
desc), bounded by the `--detail` per-thread cap. Empty vec when the
thread has no locals. Additive: not part of MAT parity.

local_root_count.description:
Number of GC-thread-local roots this thread holds that resolve to a live
object (from the dominator graph's synthetic thread→local edges). A high
count flags a thread pinning many objects alive. Additive field: not part
of MAT parity comparison. Bounded (per-thread), off the per-object budget.

max_local_retained.description:
Largest retained heap among this thread's significant local variables
(0 when frames were not computed). Mirrors MAT's "Max. Locals' Retained
Heap" column. Additive.

name.description:
Decoded `java.lang.Thread.name`, or None when the name could not be
resolved (missing thread/String, JDK layout mismatch, or empty name).
Additive field: not part of MAT parity comparison.

retained.description: Retained heap of the resolved thread object (0 when unresolved). Additive.

shallow.description: Shallow heap of the resolved thread object (0 when unresolved). Additive.

significant_frames.description:
Per-frame significant local variables, interleaved top-first. Populated
only under the opt-in `--thread-locals` flag; empty otherwise. Additive:
not part of MAT parity.

thread_serial.description: HPROF thread serial (stable within the dump).

thread_state.description:
Decoded thread state label (e.g. `[alive, runnable]`) from the raw
`threadStatus` bits. Empty when unknown. Additive.

ThreadLocalLeakRow.description:
One row of the ThreadLocal Leak Analyzer breakdown: value class name,
entry counts (total + stale), and total retained heap of the stored values.
A stale entry is one whose weak referent (the ThreadLocal key) has been
GC'd but whose value is still strongly held — a classic TL leak signal.

entry_count.description: Total number of ThreadLocalMap$Entry objects with this value class.

retained.description: Sum of retained heap across all value objects of this class.

stale_count.description: Number of entries whose key (referent) has been GC'd (stale entries).

value_class.description: Pretty class name of the stored value object.

ThreadLocalObj.description:
One sampled GC-thread-local root object held by a thread: its 1-based object
index, class name, and footprint.

ThreadOverview.description: Aggregates for the "Threads" section: one entry per resolved stack trace.

threads.description: Threads with call stacks, sorted by thread serial for determinism.

TinyCollectionRow.description: One row in the tiny-collection overhead ranking (§46.2).

TopArrayClassRow.description:
One array class in a "top array classes by aggregate shallow bytes" list.
Additive.

TopArrayRow.description: One individual array in a "top arrays by shallow bytes" list. Additive.

non_null.description:
Non-null (occupied) slot count for object arrays; `None` for primitive
arrays (every slot is always occupied). Additive.

owner.description:
Primary incoming reference (`Class#field`) that points at this array.
Resolved unconditionally from instance-dump field edges (first-wins).
`None` when no field edge references this array. Additive.

TopArrays.description:
Top arrays for one array category (primitive or object): the largest
individual arrays by shallow bytes and the largest array classes by
aggregate shallow bytes. Additive.

TopComponents.description:
Eclipse-MAT-style "Top Components": retained heap grouped by class loader
(component), with the top classes inside each. A bounded reduction over the
per-class retained aggregation (rows <= #loaders), so RSS-safe.

components.description: Components sorted by retained desc, capped to the top N.

biggest_packages.description: Root of the pruned package tree (root name = "").

size_distribution.description:
Retained-size distribution over ALL top-level dominators (additive;
not parity-compared). Empty/zero when there are no top-level dominators.

threshold_bp.description: MAT 1%-of-total pruning threshold in basis points (100 bp = 1%).

TopSizeDistribution.description:
Retained-size distribution over ALL top-level dominators (the biggest
memory contributors), bucketed by power-of-two retained size. Additive;
not parity-compared. `buckets` empty and stats zero when there are no
top-level dominators (empty heap).

TriageSeverity.description:
Severity of a fired OOM-triage signal. Currently carried for future HTML
styling (colour per severity); rule order, not severity, drives ordering.

TriageSignal.description:
One fired OOM-triage signal. Rules evaluate the finished `Report` once (see
`triage.rs`) and emit these; both the Markdown and HTML renderers are dumb
formatters over `Report.triage`, so rule logic lives in exactly one place.

`detail` may contain `` `code spans` `` in backticks: Markdown keeps them
verbatim, HTML splits them into `<code>` elements.

anchor.description: Target section id to link to, e.g. `"leak-indicators"`. `None` = no link.

bytes.description:
Reclaimable/attributable bytes this signal quantifies, when the rule has a
concrete figure (e.g. wasted collection bytes, duplicate-String waste). Used
to rank problem signals by impact; `None` for orientation signals and rules
without a byte figure. Not rendered — ordering only.

detail.description: One-sentence explanation; may contain backtick code spans.

id.description: Stable slug identifying the rule, e.g. `"off-heap"`.

nav_class.description:
Primary class name mentioned in `detail`, when there is exactly one (e.g.
the headline retainer class). Enables PivotBtn / OqlBtn in the HTML triage
panel. `None` when the signal has no single navigable class.

TypeEdge.description: One aggregated type-level reference edge for the TPFG (V13).

retained_weight.description: Sum of src-object retained / out_degree for all instances of this edge type.

top_field_names.description:
Top field names (up to 3) through which src references dst, sorted by occurrence.
Empty when field-name data was not captured (older dumps or non-instance edges).

UnreachableClassRow.description:
One row of the unreachable-objects histogram: objects that are not
dominated by the virtual root (`idom == u32::MAX`), grouped by class.
Additive; not parity-compared. Sorted by shallow descending, capped.

retained.description:
Retained size within the unreachable forest: the sum of shallow sizes of
every unreachable object dominated by objects of this class, computed by
a dominator pass over the unreachable subgraph (a synthetic root over the
garbage roots). Goes beyond MAT, which discards unreachable objects.

UnreachableGarbageRoot.description:
One node in the per-garbage-root dominator sub-tree. A garbage root is an
unreachable object that has no unreachable predecessor (entry point of a
garbage subtree). Children are capped by depth and fan-out. Additive; not
parity-compared.

objects.description: Number of real objects in the subtree rooted at this node.

pretty_class.description: Human-readable class name of the dominating object at this node.

retained.description:
Total retained heap within the subtree rooted at this node (within the
unreachable forest only).

ValueTypeShare.description: One runtime-type share within a collection's element/value tally. Additive.

count.description: Number of element slots of this type in the group.

type_name.description: Pretty runtime class name of the element/value.

VizKind.description: The declared visualization kind. `Table` is the no-op default.

VizSpec.description: A parsed `-- @viz` directive, attached to a `QueryResult`.

cap.description: Optional top-N cap for the CHART ONLY (table always shows all rows).

label_col.description: Column name (alias or derived) for the label axis; `None` => positional.

name.description:
Optional display name for the whole query block; overrides the `q{N}`
auto-label (`name="..."`).

title.description: Optional heading rendered above the chart (`title="..."`).

value_col.description: Column name for the numeric value axis; `None` => positional.

WasteBreakdownRow.description:
One row of the unified "Where Is My Memory Going?" waste breakdown
(`Report.waste_breakdown`) — derived directly from the triage `Rule`
registry (`triage::build_waste_breakdown`), one row per fired rule that
declares a `WasteCategory` and a nonzero `recoverable_bytes` figure for
this report. Unlike `WasteSummary` (a small, fixed, hand-picked set of
sources assembled directly in `build_waste_summary`), this list grows
automatically as new waste-category rules are added to the registry —
no second hand-maintained list to keep in sync. Additive; not part of
MAT parity comparison.

anchor.description: Section anchor to drill into, when the underlying signal has one.

bytes.description: Approximate reclaimable bytes this row quantifies.

rule_id.description:
The underlying triage signal's stable id (e.g. "over-capacity-collections"),
for cross-referencing against `Report.triage`.

title.description: The underlying triage signal's title (e.g. "Over-Capacity Collections").

WasteSource.description:
One reclaimable-waste source in the Waste Summary: a human label, the
approximate reclaimable bytes, and an optional anchor to the section that
details it. Additive.

anchor.description:
Canonical section slug this source drills into (e.g. "collections"),
or None when there is no dedicated section.

bytes.description: Approximate reclaimable bytes attributed to this source.

WasteSummary.description:
A single headline "reclaimable N bytes" figure folding every waste source
the report can quantify (under-filled collections & object arrays, duplicate
String values, String backing-array slack, duplicate primitive arrays). The
sources are approximate and may overlap slightly; `total_bytes` is their sum.
Present only when at least one source is nonzero. Additive; not part of MAT
parity comparison.

reachable_bytes.description:
Proportional estimate of waste attributable to reachable objects only.
Computed as `total_bytes * reachable_shallow / (reachable_shallow + unreachable_shallow)`.
Approximate because waste scans do not distinguish reachable from unreachable per-instance.

sources.description: Per-source breakdown, sorted by bytes desc. Only nonzero sources.

total_bytes.description: Sum of every source's bytes (the headline "reclaimable" figure).

description: Full report data model: only bounded aggregates, never a per-object Vec.

analysis_flags.description:
Which opt-in analysis passes were enabled. Additive; defaults to all-false
for round-trip with older JSON (which lacks the field).

arrays_by_size.description:
Power-of-two array-length histogram (object vs primitive arrays).
Always-on; additive, defaults to empty for round-trip with older JSON.

category_rollup.description:
"Classes by Category" rollup — one row per distinct category
actually present in the dump (see `CategoryRollup` docs), sorted
retained-desc. Always at least `["jdk", "other"]`-worth of rows
unless the dump is empty; grows with user-defined `[[category]]`/
`--category` entries. Additive; `#[serde(default)]` keeps older
JSON loadable.

collection_attribution.description:
Container attribution by holder `Class#field`, present only when
`--collections` was passed; `None` otherwise. Additive; not parity-compared.

collections.description:
Field-decode collection & array analysis (fill ratios, size histogram,
map collisions, constant primitive arrays). Always-on; additive,
defaults to empty for round-trip with older JSON.

dominator_analysis.description:
Dominator-tree analysis: Big Drops + Immediate Dominators. Always-on;
additive, defaults to empty for round-trip with older JSON.

field_stats.description:
Per-class reference-field statistics (null/non-null counts, total retained
of pointees). Present only when `--field-stats` was passed; `None` otherwise.

fields_by_size.description:
Holder `Class#field` ranked by total retained size of their pointees,
present only when `--collections` was passed; `None` otherwise. Additive.

finalizer_classes.description:
Per-class breakdown of live `java.lang.ref.Finalizer` instances by
referent class (P2). Empty when no Finalizers are present. Sorted by
count descending, capped at 50. Additive; `#[serde(default)]` keeps
older JSON loadable.

framework_analysis.description:
Detected framework aggregate analyses. Empty when no framework classes present.
Always-on; each entry is only emitted when its sentinel class is in the heap.
`#[serde(default)]` keeps older JSON loadable.

leak_indicators.description:
Always-computed scalar leak indicators. Additive; defaults to zero for
round-trip with older JSON.

obj_graph_flat.description: Flat object graph for V3/V4 navigation. None when --obj-graph not used.

pool_snapshots.description:
Pool state snapshots for ThreadPoolExecutor and HikariCP instances (P1).
One entry per detected pool class; instances are capped at 20 per class.
Additive; `#[serde(default)]` keeps older JSON loadable.

primary_culprits.description:
Ranked, resolved "who's actually responsible" answer(s) — computed once
from `leaks.suspects` (see `CulpritRef` docs) and consumed by the
headline triage rules instead of each re-deriving their own notion of
"the culprit" from scratch. Capped at a small handful of entries;
empty when no suspect's retained share crosses the dominance floor
(a genuinely diffuse/healthy heap — the correct answer is "no single
culprit", not a forced guess). Additive; `#[serde(default)]` keeps
older JSON loadable.

queries.description: Custom OQL query results (empty unless --query/--query-file was given).

redacted_input.description: True when the dump was produced by `hprof-analyzer redact` (primitive values zeroed).

references.description:
Soft/weak/phantom reference statistics. Always-on; additive, defaults to
empty for round-trip with older JSON.

self_referential_classes.description:
Classes detected as self-referential/recursive (a meaningful share of
instances are nested inside another instance of the same class) —
see `SelfReferentialClassRow` docs. Sorted by `total_shallow`
descending, capped at a small handful of entries. Consumed by the
`SelfReferentialClassAccumulation` triage rule; also independently
useful as a direct "which classes form recursive structures" view.
Additive; `#[serde(default)]` keeps older JSON loadable.

thread_local_analysis.description:
ThreadLocal Leak Analyzer: per-value-class breakdown of
`ThreadLocalMap$Entry` objects — entry counts, stale counts (null key),
and total retained heap. Populated only when `--find-duplicates` (or
`--full-analysis`) is passed; empty otherwise. Additive; not
parity-compared. `#[serde(default)]` keeps older JSON loadable.

top_components.description:
Eclipse-MAT-style retained-heap-by-class-loader components. Additive;
defaults to empty for round-trip with older JSON.

top_retainers.description:
Merged top-retainers: `Class#field` holders + `Class#method()` stack
frames, sorted by total retained descending, capped at 20.

triage.description:
Fired OOM-triage signals, evaluated once over the finished report by the
rule framework in `triage.rs`. Order is the registry order (render order).
`#[serde(default)]` keeps pre-v4 JSON (which lacks the field) loadable.

truncated_input.description:
True when the input dump was truncated (gzip stream ended prematurely).
The report covers only the records that were decompressed before truncation.

type_ref_graph.description: Type-level reference graph (TPFG). Present when --obj-graph is used.

waste_breakdown.description:
Unified "Where Is My Memory Going?" breakdown, derived directly from
the triage `Rule` registry (`triage::build_waste_breakdown`) — see
`WasteBreakdownRow` docs. Sorted bytes-desc. Empty when no
waste-category rule fired with a nonzero figure. Additive;
`#[serde(default)]` keeps older JSON loadable.
